description: Enable budget-protected built-in observability by default while preserving an explicit opt-out and local-only OTLP exposure.

tasks.title: Enable protected built-in observability by default
tasks.description: Align the outbound tracing, collector, and host listener-plan defaults for an absent `Mohist:Otel:Enabled` setting, while preserving explicit `false` as a full opt-out. Update Docker Compose and self-hosting documentation to inherit the default without publishing the local OTLP port, and add the focused startup, opt-out, status, and deployment-surface coverage for the complete behavior.
acceptanceCriteria: With no `Mohist:Otel:Enabled` setting, both OpenTelemetry options bindings enable their components, the host plan includes a `localhost:4318` OTLP listener, and runtime status is never `off`.
With `Mohist:Otel:Enabled=false`, the Server does not construct the tracing pipeline, bind or map the OTLP receiver, start diagnostics or maintenance work, and `mo otel status` reports `off`.
The unmodified Docker Compose configuration inherits the Server default, publishes only port `3456`, and does not publish `4318`.
Observability and self-hosting documentation state the enabled default, loopback-only receiver, resource budget, status command, and `Mohist:Otel:Enabled=false` rollback path.
Focused Server unit/spec tests cover default enablement and explicit opt-out across the options bindings, host plan, OTLP route, diagnostics sampler, and status surface; `npm test` passes.
tasks.output: Server defaults and startup composition enable protected local observability; Compose and documentation reflect the default; focused regression coverage passes.
tasks.notes: Keep the two OtelOptions types separate because they own outbound SDK and collector-specific settings respectively; only their shared enabled default and HostFactory resolution must agree. Do not alter existing budget, retention, ingest, or degradation behavior.
